name: 1811 S. Prairie Avenue — the alley building of the house at 1811 (district draft; refined by T-1936)

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 0.000, v -5.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation 179.444 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1811 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1811 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: Two storeys in 1904, where the 1911 sheet reads a '1½-storey brick GARAGE on the alley' (T-3099). The Tribune of 16 April 1904 offers the empty house to rent with a '2 story stable', and the same agents repeat it in September 1905; the Greeley-Carlson plate of 1891 draws a crossed stable marked '25' at the alley behind the house, 38-46 m from the street line where the 1911 sheet's garage stands 37-46 m; and the Chicagology photograph (after 1886; its rights unresolved, so read beside these and not cited for the count) shows it past the house's south flank as a separate pavilion with an arched carriage door under a steep roof. The plan stays the 1911 trace's. Why the 1911 sheet counts one and a half storeys no source says: the stable altered when it became a garage, or its loft counted as a roof storey, are both open.

construction.note: The trace's fabric colour on the main part: brick.

parts.from: s28fp-1811-b2 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 86% of its fill

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s28fp-1811-b2 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 86% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' overlaid with the frontage row: Romanesque: the register's 'rock-faced brown sandstone front' over 'brick side and rear', so the stone front is brownstone and the walls behind it brick; the steep Romanesque hip stands for the upper gable, whose arched lights are T-1891's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 2416702248 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-18-20-east-2330.

draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '1½-storey brick GARAGE on the alley'. 1911 labels it a garage or barn; for 1904 the envelope is backcast and its use reconstructed as a stable/coach house.

citations.citation: Greeley-Carlson Company, Atlas of the City of Chicago (Chicago, 1891), the plate covering Prairie Avenue and its environs, as reproduced by Chicagology under the caption "Prairie Avenue and Environs".

The breakwater offshore and the water's edge against the railway

what_it_does_not_supply: Measured positions: the copy is not georeferenced

citations.citation: 'To Rent—1811 Prairie-av., 16 room house; light on all sides; beautifully finished; 3 bathrooms, billiard and ball rooms; will decorate to suit tenant; 2 story stable. Holton, Seelye & Co., 204 Dearborn-st.' Classified advertisement, 'To Rent—Houses', Chicago Daily Tribune, 16 April 1904.
what_it_supplies: that 1811's alley building was a stable of two storeys in April 1904
that the house was detached, with light on all sides, and empty in spring 1904
what_it_does_not_supply: the stable's plan, roof or material

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2330, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1936 refines in place under this same id.
